claims.claim_text: The bank has identified climate-related risks affecting its lending and collateral exposures, including physical, transition, stranded asset, carbon pricing/policy, technology transition, agriculture physical, and reputational risks.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks and opportunities that could affect prospects (risk list)
claims.support_notes: Explicit list of identified climate-related risks.

claims.claim_text: Physical risk: mortgage book flood exposure is a long-term risk; flood-prone residential and commercial mortgage collateral faces rising acute physical risk that could impair collateral coverage; linked to scenario analysis SCN0009.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Physical risk — mortgage book flood exposure (long term)
claims.support_notes: Time horizon and scenario linkage stated.

claims.claim_text: Physical risk: wildfire exposure in the southern portfolio is medium term and risk rated medium; linked to scenario analysis SCN0007.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Physical risk — wildfire exposure in southern portfolio (medium term)
claims.support_notes: Risk rating and time horizon disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Transition risk: building energy performance regulation (minimum energy performance standards) may require costly retrofits for low-EPC mortgage collateral, reducing values and increasing LTV; risk rated medium; short to medium term; linked to scenario analysis SCN0011.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Transition risk — building energy performance regulation (short to medium term)
claims.support_notes: Mechanism (retrofits/value/LTV) and scenario linkage stated.

claims.claim_text: Stranded assets risk: demand shifts away from fossil fuels could strand reserves and assets held by oil, gas and coal counterparties, reducing their enterprise value; medium to long term.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Stranded assets — fossil fuel sector exposure (medium to long term)
claims.support_notes: Risk description and time horizon disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Carbon pricing and policy tightening (EU ETS and national carbon pricing) could raise operating costs for carbon-intensive borrowers and increase default probability in cement, steel and chemicals; short to medium term; linked to scenario analysis SCN0007.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Carbon pricing and policy tightening (short to medium term)
claims.support_notes: Sector examples and scenario linkage stated.

claims.claim_text: Technology transition risk (automotive): rapid electrification could strand internal-combustion vehicle manufacturers and suppliers in the lending book; medium term.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Technology transition risk (automotive) (medium term)
claims.support_notes: Risk and time horizon disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Physical risk (agriculture): chronic heat and shifting precipitation could reduce yields for agricultural counterparties and weaken repayment capacity over the medium term; linked to scenario analysis SCN0005.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Physical risk (agriculture) (medium term)
claims.support_notes: Transmission channel (yields/repayment) and scenario linkage stated.

claims.claim_text: Reputational risk: stakeholder and NGO scrutiny of financed emissions and fossil financing could damage brand and trigger client attrition; short term.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks... > Reputational risk (short term)
claims.support_notes: Risk and time horizon disclosed.

claims.claim_text: The bank has identified climate-related opportunities that could affect prospects: green loan growth (OPP-BANK01-01), sustainable bond underwriting (OPP-BANK01-02), transition advisory (OPP-BANK01-03), and renewable energy project finance (OPP-BANK01-04).
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related risks and opportunities... (opportunity list)
claims.support_notes: Opportunity list explicitly provided with IDs and time horizons.

claims.claim_text: Renewable energy project finance opportunity is aligned with REPowerEU and national renewable energy targets and includes solar, wind, and battery storage infrastructure; medium term.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Climate-related opportunities > Renewable energy project finance (OPP-BANK01-04)
claims.support_notes: Alignment statement included in text.

claims.claim_text: Climate-related risks and opportunities are concentrated in the bank’s value chain primarily through financing counterparties and collateral exposures.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Current and anticipated effects on the business model and value chain (opening paragraph)
claims.support_notes: Direct statement about concentration points in value chain.

claims.claim_text: Key concentrations include mortgage collateral in flood-prone zones, southern portfolio wildfire exposures, carbon-intensive sectors (including manufacture of coke and refined petroleum), automotive manufacturing exposures, and agricultural counterparties.
entities: manufacture of coke and refined petroleum
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Current and anticipated effects... (bullet list of concentrations)
claims.support_notes: Examples of concentration by asset type, geography, and sector.

claims.claim_text: Within the bank’s own operations, operational sites and travel generate Scope 1–2 emissions and face physical disruption, including corporate fleet and business travel.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Current and anticipated effects... (own operations sentence)
claims.support_notes: Operational boundary and emissions scopes referenced.

claims.claim_text: The bank defines time horizons for climate-related strategy and decision-making as: short term 0–3 years, medium term 3–10 years, and long term 10+ years, linked to internal planning and risk processes (budgeting, ICAAP, strategic plan, portfolio steering, and physical risk horizons including 2050 analyses).
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Time horizons used in strategic decision-making
claims.support_notes: Explicit definitions and linkage to planning processes provided.

claims.claim_text: Under orderly transition scenarios, the bank expects green loan growth and client engagement on transition plans to progressively reduce high-carbon sector concentration over the medium term.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Strategic response
claims.support_notes: Forward-looking strategic response described (expectation).

claims.claim_text: The bank has set a portfolio intensity target of 20.0 tCOe per �a3m.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Strategic response (target sentence)
claims.support_notes: Target value explicitly stated; unit appears as per �a3m in text.

claims.claim_text: The bank considers trade-offs in implementing its climate strategy, including near-term revenue vs transition risk reduction, client support vs reputational/policy risk, and growth in green assets vs concentration/execution risk.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Trade-offs considered (bullet list)
claims.support_notes: Trade-offs explicitly enumerated.

claims.claim_text: The bank assesses resilience using scenario analysis applied to the banking book.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience of strategy and business model (scenario analysis) (opening sentence)
claims.support_notes: Resilience assessment approach stated.

claims.claim_text: Orderly transition scenarios used include NGFS v4 Net Zero 2050 and Below 2�b0C (orderly), using a top-down sector-pathway approach mapping carbon price assumptions (including IEA NZE 2050 trajectory) to counterparty NACE sectors and deriving stranded asset estimates from sector-level fossil fuel capex exposure.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Orderly transition scenarios (method description)
claims.support_notes: Scenario set and methodology described.

claims.claim_text: The orderly transition scenario analysis scope covers all banking book exposures across DE, FR, IT, NL, ES.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Orderly transition scenarios (scope sentence)
claims.support_notes: Geographic scope explicitly listed.

claims.claim_text: Under orderly transition scenarios, the portfolio demonstrates adequate resilience, with transition risk losses remaining within Pillar 2 capital buffer thresholds.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Orderly transition scenarios (resilience statement)
claims.support_notes: Conclusion stated but no numeric threshold disclosed in section.

claims.claim_text: Reported revenue-at-risk includes 3,689.2m for scenario SCN0001 and 3,214.0m for a medium-term horizon.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Orderly transition scenarios (revenue-at-risk sentence)
claims.support_notes: Quantitative metric disclosed; linkage to financial effects is implied but not reconciled to financial statements here.

claims.claim_text: Disorderly transition scenarios used include NGFS v4 Divergent Net Zero, with varying carbon price assumptions by country based on national ETS and carbon tax trajectories, applied primarily to stress-test technology transition risk in the automotive and energy manufacturing lending sub-portfolio.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Disorderly transition scenarios (description)
claims.support_notes: Scenario purpose and application scope described.

claims.claim_text: Under disorderly transition scenarios, near-term resilience is acceptable, but medium-term capital consumption from stranded asset impairments is material; additional capital buffers may be required post-2030 under the most adverse disorderly assumptions.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Disorderly transition scenarios (conclusions)
claims.support_notes: Qualitative assessment; no quantified capital impact provided.

claims.claim_text: Hot house world scenarios used include NGFS v4 Current Policies and NGFS v4 NDC; physical risk parameters are sourced from NGFS hazard layers and downscaled to counterparty postcode and collateral location, using RCP 8.5 projections for a 2050 horizon analysis.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Hot house world scenarios (method description)
claims.support_notes: Data sources, downscaling approach, and horizon disclosed.

claims.claim_text: Under hot house world scenarios, physical risk losses represent the dominant long-term resilience challenge; primary transmission channels are collateral revaluation risk in flood-exposed mortgage books and agricultural borrower default risk from chronic heat stress.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Hot house world scenarios (conclusions)
claims.support_notes: Dominant challenge and channels explicitly stated.

claims.claim_text: Resilience mechanisms described include a flood-zone overlay and EPC-based collateral monitoring deployed for the 2050 horizon.
evidence_sources: draft_markdown: Strategy > Resilience... > Hot house world scenarios (resilience mechanisms sentence)
claims.support_notes: Controls/mitigations named; effectiveness not quantified.
